about: D43 (decision log): the paired, interleaved confirmation that is the verdict on "no latency regression", on the scaling report's 300,000-patient snapshot (the kept D34 build, reused unchanged), by tools/benchmark_matcher.py --paired-confirm (protocol paired-interleaved-1.0) at D41's budget policy (engine-default: every query at the engine's default search budget, 40,000), into a scratch copy of the matcher report and committed here as it was written. The reference is D42's head (0718bda, extracted from git; it lands on main unchanged), onto which this branch is rebased; the candidate is this tree, whose files the artifact digests bind. The confirmation's queries carry no count and the benchmark calls the store directly, never the dispatcher, so the two codes run byte-identical store, engine and benchmark files on this path; the run checks that nothing else moved. Earlier runs, superseded: one against 6978f43 stopped after 2.5 of 4 repeats when D41 changed the benchmark; one against f99e4f9 on the tree before the rebase onto D42, which met the rule (ratios 1.037, 1.015, 0.947, 0.995; p95 9.97 s) and whose bindings the rebase made stale (decision log, D43). The two codes run byte-identical store, engine and benchmark files: the benchmark never reaches the dispatcher.
rule: No latency regression (D43 rule 4, committed in 5781432, rebased as 93454f1): at 14 workers the paired p95 ratio (candidate over reference) is at most 1.05 in every pair, and the candidate's own 14-worker p95 is at most 10 s; the maximum, memory and the 8-worker figures are reported.

verdict.note: missed as written: the third and fourth 14-worker pairs are 1.185 and 1.064 against 1.05; the p95 bar (10 s) is met (9.56 s). Both codes ran byte-identical files on the benchmark's path, and both slowed in the third and fourth repeats (reference 8.06, 8.22, 8.18, 9.27 s; candidate 8.05, 8.22, 9.70, 9.86 s)

budget_policy.name: engine-default
budget_policy.description: every query's search_budget is 40,000: the engine's default when the field is absent and what every shipped client sends (the trajectory page, the store query page, the request examples). The query is random_query's draw with only search_budget replaced (D41).

budget_policy.name: engine-default
budget_policy.description: every query's search_budget is 40,000: the engine's default when the field is absent and what every shipped client sends (the trajectory page, the store query page, the request examples). The query is random_query's draw with only search_budget replaced (D41).

paired_confirmation.note: Each pair is the reference code and the candidate code run back to back, each in a fresh process with a warm pool, on the same snapshot and queries, each at the search budget policy its side states (budget_policy, D41); the reference runs first in even repeats and second in odd ones (ABBA). Ratios are candidate over reference: below 1 means the candidate is faster. "total" is the sum of the per-query match seconds of one run. The absolute target is judged on the candidate's own runs in this session. The pairing cancels drift that is slow against the length of a pair (minutes); it does not cancel noise within a run, nor a difference that only one order shows (compare the reference-first and candidate-first pairs).

limitations: one machine and one session; synthetic data replicated beyond 10,000 patients; the p95 of 30 queries is the second-slowest query; the paired protocol cancels slow drift, not noise inside a run; no count request is timed here (a 1.3 Event frequency request at 300,000 is reported apart in the decision log)
